title: AGN impact on the molecular gas in galactic centres as probed by CO lines
question: What is the relative contribution of far-ultraviolet radiation from star formation (PDRs) and X-ray radiation from active galactic nuclei (XDRs) to the molecular gas heating and CO line excitation in local active galaxies?

what.value: Herschel SPIRE-FTS CO line fluxes (J=4-3 to 13-12)

evidence.quote: We collect SPIRE data from (cite: rosenberg15; mashian15; pearson16; kame16; lu17), which altogether account for CO fluxes from 226 galaxies.

what.value: X-ray luminosities, column densities N_H, and photon indices

evidence.quote: The data are taken from (cite: ricci17), (cite: marchesi19; lacaria19) and Salvestrini et al. (2022, in prep.). When not available in these works, we take the $L_{\text{X}}$ and $N_{\text{H}}$ derived from *XMM-Newton* in the 0.5–10 keV band by (cite: brightman11).

external_data.citation: (cite: ricci17), (cite: marchesi19; lacaria19), Salvestrini et al. (2022, in prep.), (cite: brightman11)

what.value: Low-J CO fluxes from single-dish observations in the literature

evidence.quote: All the CO line luminosities are taken from (cite: rosenberg15; mashian15; pearson16; kame16; lu17) unless otherwise specified.

external_data.citation: (cite: papadopoulos12; curran01; evans05; salome11; mao10; xia12; maiolino97; israel20; dumas10; rigopoulou97; pereira13; espada19; israel92; gao99; alloin92; albrecht07; gao04; ueda14; imanishi17; rosario18; monje11; young95)

evidence.quote: L$_{\text{IR}}$ is the 8–1000 $\mu$m luminosity, from (cite: sanders03) unless otherwise specified.

what.value: Comparison galaxy samples for the Schmidt-Kennicutt relation (starbursts, BASS AGN, xCOLD GASS, SLUGS)

evidence.loc: CO emission on global galactic scales
evidence.quote: comparing them with starburst (SB) galaxies from (cite: k21) (K21, hereafter), AGN observed with Swift/BAT from the BASS sample (cite: ricci17), star-forming galaxies (SFG) from the xCOLD GASS survey (cite: saintonge17), and IR luminous galaxies from SLUGS (cite: dunne00). The latter three samples were gathered by (cite: lamperti20) (L20, hereafter).

what.value: ALMA CO(6-5) flux of NGC 34 at 200 mas resolution (707 +/- 106 Jy km s^-1)

evidence.quote: The total flux of the CO(6–5) detection with a resolution of 200 mas is $S_{\text{CO(6--5)}} = 707 \pm 106$ Jy km s$^{-1}$, obtained by (cite: mingozzi18), using CASA 4.5.2 (cite: mcmullin07) and a natural weighting scheme.

recipe.goal: Measure the size and flux of nuclear CO(6-5) emission from ALMA archival cubes
recipe.method: Retrieve calibrated and cleaned CO(6-5) data cubes from the ALMA Archive for 7 sample galaxies, generate moment 0 maps using CASA task immoments, fit a 2D Gaussian with task imfit (for NGC 34 high-res data), and measure the radial extent of the CO(6-5) emitting region.
key_parameters: median nuclear radius r = 250 pc adopted as upper limit for J >= 6 emitting region
assumptions: Higher-J CO lines (J >= 6) originate from a region at most as extended as CO(6-5) (r = 250 pc)

recipe.goal: Derive galactic-scale CO(1-0) fluxes, molecular gas masses, SFRs, and Schmidt-Kennicutt relation
recipe.method: Extrapolate single-dish CO(1-0) beam fluxes to the CO scale radius r_CO using a 3D exponential disk profile, compute molecular gas mass M_mol, integrate Herschel/PACS 70 um radial profiles up to r_CO to obtain SFR, and compare Sigma_mol and Sigma_SFR on the Schmidt-Kennicutt plane.
key_parameters: X_CO = 2 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (alpha_CO = 4.3 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^-2)^-1)
assumptions: CO(1-0) emission follows a 3D exponential profile in r and z
Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor applies, and 70 um emission traces star formation with negligible AGN contamination

recipe.goal: Calculate nuclear (r <= 250 pc) CO line ratios, FUV radiation field G_0, and X-ray flux F_X, and fit correlations
recipe.method: Scale CO(1-0) flux down to r <= 250 pc using the 3D exponential profile while keeping J >= 6 fluxes unaltered; fit Sersic profiles to Herschel/PACS 70 um maps to evaluate G_0 at r = 250 pc; compute F_X = L_X / (4 pi r^2), H_X, and xi_eff at r = 250 pc; perform Bayesian linear regression of CO line ratios against G_0 and F_X using Linmix.
assumptions: All FUV photons are absorbed by dust and re-emitted at 70 um
CO(6-5) and higher-J lines are fully confined within r = 250 pc

recipe.goal: Compare observed nuclear CO line ratios with CLOUDY PDR and XDR model grids
recipe.method: Overlay observed CO line ratios (relative to CO(1-0) and CO(6-5)) as a function of G_0 and F_X onto 1-D slab CLOUDY PDR and XDR model grids computed across gas densities log(n/cm^-3) = [2, 3, 4, 5] to constrain gas density and heating mechanism.
assumptions: Both numerator and denominator CO lines in each ratio originate from the same area so single-cloud slab ratios can be compared to galaxy nuclear ratios

evidence.quote: To estimate the flux, we performed a 2D Gaussian fit with the task `imfit`, which returned $62 \pm 3$ Jy km s$^{-1}$, less than $10 \%$ of the total flux measured by SPIRE-FTS ($920 \pm 56$ Jy km s$^{-1}$).
The emission consists of a single clump of $r \lesssim 50$ pc.

However, per-galaxy inclinations, Sersic fit parameters for G_0, and CASA immoments channel ranges are not tabulated, requiring re-fitting of Herschel 70 um images and manual inspection of ALMA cubes.
